newsitem.title: USA: MOODY'S AFFIRMS ZURICH INSURANCE RATINGS.
newsitem.headline: MOODY'S AFFIRMS ZURICH INSURANCE RATINGS.

text.p: NEW YORK, June 30 - Moody's Investors Service on Monday said it confirmed its Aa1 insurance financial strength rating of Zurich Insurance Co.
Moody's also said it confirmed the debt and financial strength ratings of various of Zurich's subsidiaries, as detailed below.

The rating confirmations were made in connection with the announcement made by Zurich that it has entered into a definitive agreement with Scudder, Stevens & Clark (Scudder), an investment management firm based in New York, to effectively merge their fund management operations.
The confirmation reflects Moody's view of the fundamental strengths of the Zurich Insurance Company as the parent of a number of successful companies in the areas of risk and investment management.

Moody's stated that Zurich Insurance Company is strongly positioned in the Swiss and European nonlife insurance markets, and that its property and casualty insurance subsidiaries have also attained defensible positions in other countries. Its life assurance subsidiaries are prominent in Switzerland and Germany.

In addition, its reinsurance subsidiaries located in Europe, the United States and Bermuda, are among the leading and most innovative global reinsurers. The United States has been a main territory for the Zurich Insurance Group, where it has been been developing its operations organically and through a string of acquisitions.

Fund management has been a core business since the early 1990s, and has been given a thrust in the last two years, first through the acquisition of the Kemper Corporation and subsidiaries, and now through this merger with Scudder.

Moody's noted that although the transaction with Scudder again impacts the financial profile of Zurich, the existing ratings have hitherto reflected Moody's expectation that, following the acquisition of Kemper, the group would need to seek further expansion in order to achieve presence in the competitive global fund management market.

Offsetting the financial impact of the transaction, the rating agency noted, is the consistent and, in many cases rising, profitability of most of Zurich's companies, which gives Zurich financial stability to implement its strategy.

The rating outlook, however, is negative in view of the increasingly aggressive capital structure of the group, the expectation that further expansion by acquisition may ensue and the extremely competitive environments in which all the group's companies operate.

The ratings of Zurich Reinsurance Centre, Inc. -- Aa3 insurance financial strength -- and Zurich Reinsurance Centre Holdings, Inc. -- A1 senior unsecured debt-- remain under review for possible upgrade.
These ratings were placed under review on 13 January 1997 following the announcement that Zurich Insurance intended to acquire all the minority interests of its subsidiary.
The following ratings were confirmed:
Zurich Insurance Company -- Aa1 insurance financial strength.
Alpina Insurance Company Limited -- Aa1 insurance financial strength.
Zurich Insurance (Jersey) Limited -- Aa3 guaranteed subordinated debentures.
Zurich Life Insurance Company of America -- Aa3 insurance financial strength.
Federal Kemper Life Assurance Company -- Aa3 insurance financial strength.
Kemper Investors Life Insurance Company -- Aa3 insurance financial strength.
Kemper Corporation -- A1 senior unsecured debt, A1 senior unsecured medium-term notes, and "a1" preferred stock.
Zurich Holding Company of America, Inc. -- Aa3 junior subordinated debentures.
Zurich Capital Trust I -- "aa2" capital securities.
The following ratings remain under review for possible upgrade:
Zurich Reinsurance Centre, Inc. -- Aa3 insurance financial strength.
Zurich Reinsurance Centre Holdings, Inc. -- A1 senior unsecured debt.

Zurich Insurance Company, based in Zurich, Switzerland, is a leading nonlife insurer and reinsurer with significant operations in nonlife insurance, reinsurance, life assurance and fund management. In 1996, the group wrote total gross premiums in excess of Sfr 31 billion. At year-end 1996, the Zurich Group reported consolidated assets of Sfr 131 billion, and shareholders' funds of Sfr 13.7 billion. Monday, 30 June 1997 18:42:08 ENDS nN30528877
